items.pronunciation_notes: The ह is a light breath and the stress falls on the long second syllable: ha-vaa.

learn.title_en: The second feminine noun ending in -ा
learn.explanation_en: हवा means wind or air, and like चिंता two levels back it ends in -ा and is feminine. That is now two in fifteen words, which is enough to treat as a real category rather than a freak case: a small set of nouns ends in -ा without being masculine, and there is no way to tell from looking. The consequence is visible immediately — ठंडी हवा, not ठंडा, and the plural is हवाएँ rather than हवे. Its verb is चलना, to move: हवा चल रही है, the wind is blowing.

examples.note: रही agrees with the feminine हवा.
The adjective is feminine, which is the proof that हवा is.
नहीं in its usual place in front of the verb.

common_error.why_en: The -ा ending misleads. हवा is feminine, so a marked adjective in front of it takes -ी.

practice.question: हवा
practice.explanation_en: हवा is wind or air, and it is feminine despite the -ा ending.

game.explanation_en: हवा चलना — the wind moves. चलना is the verb Hindi uses for anything that runs or travels.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both consonants are retroflex, with the tongue curled back for the ठ and the ड: ṭhanḍ.

learn.title_en: ठंड for the weather, ठंडा for the thing
learn.explanation_en: ठंड is the cold — the condition outside — and it is a feminine noun. ठंडा is the adjective meaning cold, and it agrees like any marked adjective: ठंडा पानी, ठंडी हवा. Keep them apart and a whole set of sentences opens up. The verb is लगना, the same one that goes with डर, and the person feeling it takes को: मुझे ठंड लग रही है, I am feeling cold. Not मैं ठंड हूँ, which would say you are the cold weather.

examples.note: रही agrees with ठंड, which is feminine.
The weather stated plainly, with होना.
The adjective ठंडा, agreeing with the masculine पानी.

common_error.why_en: That sentence says you are the cold weather. The feeling attaches to you, so मुझे and लगना.

practice.question: ठंड
practice.explanation_en: ठंड is the cold. ठंडा is the adjective meaning a cold thing.

game.explanation_en: ठंड लगना — cold attaches to you, exactly as डर does.

items.pronunciation_notes: The र is rolled lightly against the म that follows: gar-mii.

learn.title_en: गर्मी is heat, गर्मियाँ is summer
learn.explanation_en: गर्मी is heat, feminine and predictable from its -ी ending. The interesting part is the plural: गर्मियाँ means the summer, the season, rather than several heats. Hindi does that with a few weather words — the plural names the time of year. So गर्मियों में means in the summer, with the oblique plural before में exactly as Module 6 would predict. Its verb is लगना, like ठंड, and गरम is the adjective for a hot thing.

examples.note: The same shape as ठंड लग रही है.

examples.hindi: गर्मियों में बहुत गर्मी होती है
examples.read_as: garmiyoṁ meṁ bahut garmii hotii hai
examples.english: it is very hot in the summer
examples.note: गर्मियों is the oblique plural before में.
गरम is unmarked, so it never changes.

common_error.why_en: For the season Hindi uses the plural, and before में that plural goes oblique: गर्मियों.

practice.question: गर्मी
practice.explanation_en: गर्मी is heat, and its plural गर्मियाँ names the summer.

game.explanation_en: गर्मी लगना — heat attaches to you. गर्मी होना describes the weather rather than your feeling.

tts_strings: गर्मियों में बहुत गर्मी होती है

summary.recap_en: हवा is the second feminine noun in this module to end in -ा, which makes it a category rather than an oddity. ठंड and गर्मी both take लगना for the feeling and होना for the weather, and each has a separate adjective — ठंडा and गरम — for describing a thing.
summary.next_up_en: Next: clouds, the sky, and the word that covers both weather and season.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long aa in the first syllable and a very light second: baa-dal.

learn.explanation_en: बादल is a cloud, masculine, and Class 2 — so it does not change in the singular and takes बादलों before a postposition in the plural. Its collocation is छाना, a verb meaning to spread over or cover: बादल छाए हैं, the sky has clouded over. That is a genuinely idiomatic pairing and worth learning whole, because none of the obvious guesses works. Clouds do not come and they do not happen; they spread.

examples.note: The perfective with a plural subject — छाना is intransitive.

examples.english: there are clouds in the sky
examples.note: आसमान is oblique before में, though nothing visible changes.
The adjective is plural masculine, agreeing with बादल.

common_error.why_en: आना would suggest the clouds travelled here as visitors. Hindi uses छाना for the sky filling up.

practice.question: बादल
practice.explanation_en: बादल is a cloud, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: बादल छाना — the clouds spread across the sky.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable holds a diphthong close to the vowel in English 'how': mau-sam.

learn.title_en: One word for weather and season both
learn.explanation_en: मौसम covers what English splits between weather and season, and context does the separating: आज मौसम अच्छा है is about today, while बारिश का मौसम is the rainy season. It is masculine and flagged, since the consonant ending predicts nothing. The verb is बदलना, to change, which is intransitive here — मौसम बदल रहा है, the weather is changing — so no ने is involved anywhere.

examples.note: अच्छा agrees with the masculine मौसम.
The continuous present, with मौसम as the subject.
का agrees with मौसम, the thing possessed, exactly as Module 6 taught.

common_error.why_en: का agrees with the thing possessed, and मौसम is masculine. That बारिश is feminine changes nothing.

practice.question: मौसम
practice.explanation_en: मौसम is weather, and also season depending on context.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long aa vowels bracketing a light middle: aas-maan.

collocation.english: for the sky to be clear

learn.title_en: आसमान — where all the weather happens
learn.explanation_en: आसमान is the sky, masculine, a Persian borrowing, and flagged because nothing about it predicts gender. It is the word every other item in this block sits inside: बादल आसमान में छाते हैं, धूप आसमान से आती है. The phrase worth having whole is आसमान साफ़ है, the sky is clear, where साफ़ is an unmarked adjective and so does not change. Note that साफ़ carries a dot under the फ़ and is pronounced with an f.

examples.note: साफ़ is unmarked and never changes.
आसमान is oblique before में — Class 2, so it shows nothing.
नीला is marked and agrees with the masculine आसमान.

common_error.why_en: आसमान is masculine, so a marked adjective takes -ा. The consonant ending gives you no help, which is why it is flagged.

practice.question: आसमान
practice.explanation_en: आसमान is the sky, and it is masculine.

game.question_en: Which adjective goes with आसमान to say the sky is clear?
game.explanation_en: आसमान साफ़ है — a clear sky. साफ़ is unmarked, so it never changes.

summary.recap_en: बादल छाना, मौसम बदलना, आसमान साफ़ होना — three more pairings that no rule predicts. All three nouns are masculine, all three are flagged, and all three are Class 2, so nothing about them changes in the singular.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the nature words — tree, river and flower — and the verbs that go with living things.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ड़ is a flap, made by striking the curled tongue once against the roof of the mouth: peṛ.

learn.title_en: पेड़ लगाना — you attach a tree to the ground
learn.explanation_en: पेड़ is a tree, masculine and flagged. Its verb is लगाना, which is the transitive partner of लगना — the same लगना that goes with डर and ठंड. Where लगना means something attaches by itself, लगाना means someone attaches it, and for a tree that comes out as planting. Because लगाना is transitive, its perfective needs the ने construction, so for now use it in the habitual, the continuous, the future or the imperative.

examples.note: The habitual present, which is safe with a transitive verb.
The oblique plural before a compound postposition.
The adjective is plural masculine; पेड़ itself does not change.

common_error.why_en: लगना would mean the tree attaches itself. Someone has to plant it, so the transitive लगाना is needed.

practice.question: पेड़
practice.explanation_en: पेड़ is a tree, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with पेड़ when someone plants one?
game.explanation_en: पेड़ लगाना. लगाना is the transitive form — someone does it — while लगना happens by itself.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two light syllables with the length on the second: na-dii.

learn.explanation_en: नदी is a river, feminine and predictable from its -ी ending, and it declines exactly like लड़की from Module 6: नदी में in the singular, नदियों में in the plural. After several flagged words in a row this one is a relief — everything about it follows a rule you already have. Its verb is बहना, to flow, which is intransitive, so all of Module 7's tenses are available: नदी बह रही है, नदी बही.

examples.note: रही agrees with the feminine नदी.

examples.english: there is water in the river
examples.note: नदी is Class 4, so the singular oblique shows nothing.
The oblique plural takes -ियों, exactly as लड़कियों does.

common_error.why_en: The long ी shortens and a य appears before the ending. This is the Class 4 plural from Module 6, unchanged.

practice.question: नदी
practice.explanation_en: नदी is a river, feminine, and it declines like लड़की.

game.explanation_en: नदी बहना — a river flows. चलना is for things that travel, not for water.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated ph with a real puff of air, not the f of English: phuul.

learn.title_en: फूल, and the ph that is not an f
learn.explanation_en: फूल is a flower, masculine and flagged. The pronunciation is worth pausing on: फ is an aspirated p, so फूल begins with a puff of air rather than with the f of English flower. The dotted फ़ is the one that sounds like f, and the two are different letters. Its verb is खिलना, to bloom, which is intransitive and also used of people — उसका चेहरा खिल गया means her face lit up.

examples.note: रहे is plural, agreeing with फूल used as a plural.
लाल is unmarked, so it works for singular and plural alike.

examples.english: there are flowers on the tree
examples.note: पेड़ is oblique before पर, though Class 2 shows nothing.

common_error.why_en: होना would simply say a flower exists. खिलना is the verb for the act of opening, and it is what pairs with फूल.

practice.question: फूल
practice.explanation_en: फूल is a flower, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

summary.recap_en: The weather and nature block is complete at twelve words. Nine of the twelve are gender-flagged, because weather and landscape nouns almost all end in consonants — which makes this the block where the memorised gender matters most and the ending helps least.
summary.next_up_en: Next: travel and transport, starting with the words you need to get anywhere at all.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f, so this is safar and not saphar: sa-far.

learn.title_en: सफ़र — the journey, not the destination
learn.explanation_en: सफ़र is a journey or a trip, masculine and flagged. It is a Persian borrowing with a dotted फ़, so it is pronounced with an f — compare फूल from the last level, which has a plain फ and a puff of air. The verb is करना, so सफ़र करना is to travel. Since करना is transitive, its perfective needs ने, which means for now you can say मैं सफ़र करता हूँ and मैं सफ़र करूँगा but not yet I travelled.

examples.note: The habitual present, safe with a transitive verb.
अच्छा and था both agree with the masculine सफ़र.
लंबा is marked and agrees with सफ़र.

common_error.why_en: सफ़र is masculine. Nothing in the word says so, which is why it carries a flag.

practice.question: सफ़र
practice.explanation_en: सफ़र is a journey, masculine, and pronounced with an f.

game.explanation_en: सफ़र करना — to travel. A journey is something you do.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ड़ is a flap between two long vowels: gaa-ṛii.
items.gloss_en: vehicle — a car, a train, anything that carries you

learn.title_en: गाड़ी covers far more than car
learn.explanation_en: गाड़ी is any wheeled vehicle that carries people — a car, a train, a cart, a van. Context does the narrowing, and रेलगाड़ी exists if you need to be specific about a train. It is feminine and predictable from the -ी, and it declines like नदी. The verb is चलाना, the transitive partner of चलना: where चलना means to move or run by itself, चलाना means someone makes it move, so it covers driving and operating anything.

examples.note: चलाती agrees with the subject वह, not with गाड़ी.
The intransitive चलना, with गाड़ी as the subject.
से marks the means of travel.

common_error.why_en: चलती would mean she herself is moving. Driving is something done to the vehicle, so the transitive चलाना is needed.

practice.question: गाड़ी
practice.explanation_en: गाड़ी is any vehicle that carries you — car, train or cart.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with गाड़ी when a person drives it?
game.explanation_en: गाड़ी चलाना. चलना is what the vehicle does by itself; चलाना is what the driver does to it.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both t sounds are retroflex, which is how English words get absorbed into Hindi: ṭi-kaṭ.

learn.title_en: An English word, absorbed and re-sounded
learn.explanation_en: टिकट is a ticket, borrowed from English and written with retroflex ट rather than the dental त — which is what happens to almost every English t that enters Hindi. It is masculine, flagged, and Class 2, so nothing changes in the singular. The verb is लेना, to take, which is how Hindi says buy for small purchases. लेना is transitive and its perfective is लिया, one of the four forms Module 7 taught as recognition only, so for now use the future or the habitual.

examples.note: The future, which is safe with any verb.
मिलना means to be available, and it is intransitive.
Class 2, so the plural looks identical to the singular.

common_error.why_en: करना is the default guess and it is wrong here. Hindi takes a ticket rather than doing one.

practice.question: टिकट
practice.explanation_en: टिकट is a ticket, masculine, and written with retroflex consonants.

game.explanation_en: टिकट लेना — you take a ticket. करना would be the natural English guess and it is not what Hindi says.

summary.recap_en: Three travel words and three different verbs — सफ़र करना, गाड़ी चलाना, टिकट लेना. Note the pattern behind चलना and चलाना: the second form of a verb, with a long aa inserted, means someone makes it happen rather than it happening by itself.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the road, the bus, and a conversation about how you are getting there.

items.pronunciation_notes: The स and त run together with no vowel between: raas-taa.

learn.explanation_en: रास्ता is a road or a way, masculine and predictable from its -ा ending, which also makes it Class 1 from Module 6 — so it becomes रास्ते before a postposition and रास्तों in the oblique plural. After a run of Class 2 nouns that never change, this one does, and it is worth the practice. The verb is पूछना, to ask: रास्ता पूछो, ask the way. It also means way in the abstract sense, as in a way of doing something.

examples.note: The तुम imperative, and रास्ता is the object rather than oblique.
Class 1, so the -ा becomes -े before में.
लंबा agrees with the masculine रास्ता.

common_error.why_en: रास्ता ends in -ा, so it is Class 1 and must go oblique before a postposition.

practice.question: रास्ता
practice.explanation_en: रास्ता is a road or way, masculine, and it declines like लड़का.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with रास्ता when you are lost?
game.explanation_en: रास्ता पूछना — to ask the way.

items.pronunciation_notes: One short syllable, identical in sound to the other बस meaning enough: bas.

learn.title_en: बस is feminine, and it is also a different word
learn.explanation_en: बस the vehicle is feminine — worth memorising, because the English original gives you nothing and neither does the ending. That gender shows up the moment an adjective appears: बस सस्ती है, not सस्ता. There is also a second बस in Hindi, entirely unrelated, meaning enough or just: बस, इतना ही, that is all. Same spelling, same sound, and context separates them without difficulty. The verb is पकड़ना, to catch or grab.

examples.note: The तुम imperative from Module 7.
सस्ती is feminine, which proves बस is.
से marks the means, and बस is oblique before it.

common_error.why_en: बस is feminine, so a marked adjective takes -ी. English speakers default to masculine here because the word looks foreign.

practice.question: बस
practice.explanation_en: बस is a bus, and it is feminine. A second बस means enough.

game.explanation_en: बस पकड़ना — to catch a bus, exactly as English does.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two short syllables running together: bas-se.

learn.title_en: से for how you are getting there
learn.explanation_en: To say by bus, by car, by train, Hindi uses से — the same postposition that means from. बस से, गाड़ी से, ट्रेन से. There is no separate word for by, and the noun goes oblique in front of it as usual, though with बस and गाड़ी nothing visible changes. Watch the last line of this exchange: सस्ती is feminine because बस is, and that is the only thing in the conversation that could go wrong.

common_error.why_en: में would mean inside the bus as a location. For the means of travel Hindi uses से.

practice.question: बस से
practice.explanation_en: से marks the means of travel. The same word also means from, and context separates them.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: बस is feminine, so the adjective is सस्ती.

summary.recap_en: रास्ता is Class 1 and goes oblique before a postposition, which most travel nouns so far have not. बस is feminine even though it is borrowed from English, and से is how Hindi says by when it comes to getting somewhere.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the station, the plane and the words for arriving, which complete the travel block.
